name: Juggling tricks beyond the basic cascade
blurb: Once the cascade is automatic, a handful of variations turn “I can juggle” into something worth watching: columns, under-the-leg, over-the-top and the start of a shower.
steps: Get the cascade truly boring first — 100 catches without thought.
Learn reverse cascade, throwing over the top of the incoming ball instead of under it. Practise it one ball at a time.
Learn columns: two balls going straight up and down on the outside, one in the middle, no crossing.
Learn under-the-leg with a single ball, then insert it into the cascade once per cycle.
Learn the two-in-one-hand pattern with your dominant hand — this is the gateway to almost every harder trick.
Chain three tricks into a short routine with a clean start and a deliberate finish.
tips: Every new pattern briefly wrecks your cascade. That is normal, and it comes back better.
Learn tricks on both sides from the start; retrofitting your weak hand later is miserable.
proof: You juggle for a minute, dropping in three different tricks, without breaking the pattern.
